text:
incident-bot: SEV-2 ALERT — HelixFin (enterprise VPC / dedicated-pool-4) reported: sudden KV prefix cache hit-rate collapse on tenant helix-prod. Hit-rate dropped ~85% -> 2% in ~3m. Increased tail latency for text-gen requests, customer-visible errors ~1.8% :rotating_light:

jamie_oncall: on it. paging eng-runtime and SRE. tagging @mike_runtime @ana_sre

ana_sre: I'm on-call. first quick checks: Grafana shows spike in evictions and TTL churn right before the drop. CPU on pool nodes fine, but KV metadata ops spiked.

mike_runtime: looking at runtime logs now. seeing lots of "namespace-marked-invalid" events and repeated prefix re-registration failures. possible metadata corruption or a bad client TTL loop.

jamie_oncall: can we confirm whether this is tenant-level cache disabled or global? customer reported they rolled out a batch job around the time window. lucy_customer_sre — any customer-side changes?

lucy_customer_sre: customer confirmed: rolling prefix-rewrite job at 15:02 UTC that touches ~120k prefixes. They expected a short backfill; didn't expect to touch cache TTLs.

mike_runtime: aha. logs show a churn loop where a client writes leases with 0 TTL repeatedly. our eviction manager treats 0 as immediate expiry and also triggers aggressive re-registration which overloads the prefix indexing. snippet:```
[2026-03-15T15:03:07Z] prefix=helix-prod/txn-09 action=lease_write ttl=0 result=OK
[2026-03-15T15:03:07Z] prefix=helix-prod/txn-09 action=evict trigger=ttl_zero
[2026-03-15T15:03:07Z] prefix=helix-prod/txn-09 action=re-register status=throttle
```

jamie_oncall: impact: customer p50 latency +40ms, p99 +620ms, errors up from 0.2% -> 1.8%. Risk: other tenants in dedicated-pool-4 share the global prefix index; isolation boundary weak here.

ana_sre: mitigation plan (short):
- TEMP: add per-tenant cache bypass for helix-prod to stop churn hitting shared index (will route their requests without hitting prefix cache).
- MED: apply an admission filter on lease_write for ttl==0 to reject/batch with backoff at ingress for that tenant.
- LONG: patch eviction manager to avoid immediate re-register loops for 0-ttl churn and add per-tenant namespace quota.

jamie_oncall: executing TEMP now. running command:```bash
# throttle cache reads for tenant helix-prod in pool 4
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/pools/4/tenants/helix-prod/cache_bypass -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"enable":true}'
```

devops-bot: action accepted. cache_bypass enabled for tenant helix-prod on pool 4 at 1835007789.

mike_runtime: after bypass, observing hit-rate stabilize for other tenants; helix-prod requests routing to direct KVS reads (higher cost but steady). latency for other tenants back to normal.

lucy_customer_sre: passing this to HelixFin: "we've put a temporary bypass in place to stop cache churn; this may increase your token cost/latency slightly while we fix the root cause. please pause the backfill job if possible."

toni_account: drafted message to HelixFin CSM + engineering: "Mitigated immediate impact; engineering working on durable fix; will follow up with RCA and timeline."

mike_runtime: quick notes on root cause hypothesis: the customer's backfill inadvertently wrote leases with ttl=0; our eviction path treats ttl=0 as explicit eviction and triggers immediate re-registration which creates a tight loop and saturates the prefix index locking path. two problems: (1) we re-register synchronously, holding global index locks; (2) no tenant write rate limit on metadata ops.

jamie_oncall: next steps assigned:
- @mike_runtime: implement admission filter + hotfix to treat 0-ttl as no-op or queue (ETA 2h).
- @ana_sre: monitor pool metrics and validate isolation after bypass (ETA 30m).
- @lucy_customer_sre: coordinate with HelixFin to pause job and confirm post-bypass perf (ETA 15m).
- @toni_account: prepare customer comms and escalation thread for account execs (ETA 1h).

ana_sre: note: I'll handoff in 40m. if hotfix not merged by then, please escalate to oncall-2.

jamie_oncall: thanks. quick handoff to oncall-2 if needed. summary for next oncall:
- incident: KV prefix cache hit-rate collapse caused by tenant backfill writing ttl=0 leases -> eviction/re-register loop.
- mitigation: enabled tenant cache_bypass for helix-prod (timestamp 1835007789). Other tenants stable.
- customer impact: higher latency/cost for helix-prod; broader pool impact mitigated.
- actions: admission-filter hotfix by eng-runtime, add per-tenant metadata rate limits, long-term rework of eviction re-register logic.

jamie_oncall: ana — please paste any additional logs before you go.

ana_sre: extra logs:```
[2026-03-15T15:04:02Z] pool=4 prefix_ops_pending=842 lock_wait_ms=312
[2026-03-15T15:04:05Z] evict_loop_detected tenant=helix-prod loops=27 backoff_applied=false
[2026-03-15T15:04:12Z] cache_bypass applied tenant=helix-prod result=ok
```

mike_runtime: will open a PR for hotfix -> tagging @jamie_oncall for review. PR link: https://git.internal.redwood/pr/runner/4521 (will update when created).

lucy_customer_sre: HelixFin paused job. they asked for ETA on full fix; I told them 2-4 hours for hotfix + testing.

toni_account: adding meeting with HelixFin engineering in 30m to walk mitigations.

jamie_oncall: wrapping up handoff. if oncall-2 picks this up, summary above + link to logs/grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/kv/pool4?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall shift end for ana_sre in 40m. auto-reminder set.

jamie_oncall: thanks everyone. keep thread for updates. :v:
